observations: Photos 0-2 show stacks of wooden pallets outdoors on bare dirt mixed with trash and debris.
Photo 2 shows several pallet blocks stamped 'EPAL', indicating genuine or branded Euro-pallets.
Photo 1 shows pallets with darker, rougher blocks that look different in color/texture from the EPAL ones in photo 2, suggesting a mixed batch of pallet types or ages.
Photo 3 shows a single pallet held up by two hands; it has cracked, split boards, visible staining/discoloration, and no visible stamp or brand mark.
No photo shows a scale, weighbridge ticket, or any document supporting the 500kg weight claim.
No close-up of wood grain or block material to confirm 'dry, no water added' claim.
Seller's new message repeats the original claims verbally but adds no new photo or document.

Close-up photos of stamps/markings (EPAL, IPPC, heat-treatment HT mark) on each pallet or a representative sample
